Given a $2\times 2$ matrix

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}],
$$

the inverse of $C$ can be found using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{det(C)}[\begin{aligned}d & -b \\ -c & a\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

First, we compute the determinant:

$$
det(C)=3\cdot 0-1\cdot 3=-3
$$

Using the formula, then, the inverse is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{det(C)}[\begin{aligned}d & -b \\ -c & a\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{(-3)}[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can verify the result as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}C{C}^{-1} & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{2}\,✓ \\ {C}^{-1}C & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{2}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
